name: Propellers
description: A propeller pushes air and the ship pushes back.

pages.title: Propellers
pages.text: A propeller pushes air and the ship pushes back. A Propeller [#](7A3C9A)[Bearing](entry://glossary/bearing)[#]() spins a structure of sails. Any structure with at least **two sail-like blocks** counts, and more sails give more thrust.

pages.title: Propeller Bearing
pages.text: Attaches to the block in front. Reversing rotation reverses thrust; a [#](2E5AAC)[wrench](entry://create_basics/tools_wrench)[#]() does too. Goggles show thrust and airflow.

pages.title: Gyroscopic Propeller Bearing
pages.text: Keeps its propeller upright, for helicopters. Facing down it steadies top-heavy ships. Redstone resets the tilt.

pages.title: Smart Propeller
pages.text: Makes thrust when spun and tilts along one axis to try to face upward. A wrench reverses its thrust.

pages.title: Wooden Propeller
pages.text: A ready-made small propeller. The Andesite Propeller is its sturdier twin.

pages.title: Limits
pages.text: A propeller already moving through air pushes less, because the air is moving too. Thrust also fades with altitude, and props are of little use where there is no air.

pages.title: Fast enough to fly
pages.text:
A propeller pushes only up to its **airflow** speed: a tenth of its RPM for a Wooden or Andesite Propeller, 0.05 x the square root of its sails x RPM for a Propeller Bearing.\
\
A plane must pass its take-off speed below that, so spin its propellers at 256 RPM, the most a shaft turns: 25.6 blocks a second.

pages.title: Gearing up
pages.text:
Each large cogwheel driving a small one doubles the speed, so a Portable Engine's 32 RPM takes three such steps to reach 256.\
\
At 256 RPM a Wooden Propeller draws 1024 stress units, so one Portable Engine turns two of them.

pages.title: Big fans
pages.text:
A Propeller Bearing pushes 0.2 x sails^1.5 x RPM for 2 stress units per sail per RPM, so a big fan pushes more for the same engines: 13 sails at 128 RPM push 1200, more than four Wooden Propellers at 256 RPM.\
\
Two Portable Engines on one shaft at the same speed add up their stress and turn one such fan.

pages.title: Through gearboxes
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** a gearbox turns its straight-through side the other way from its sideways sides. Propellers fed through different gearbox faces can push against each other.\
\
Watch which way each one blows, and wrench the front of any that pushes backward to reverse it.

pages.title: Sail wings
pages.text:
Create sails lift like Wing blocks at a quarter of the weight, so early planes fly on sail wings. Two wings stacked on struts double the lift.\
\
Allow about three sails facing up per full block's weight in the rest: a plank weighs half a block; a slab, fence or trapdoor a quarter.

pages.title: Symmetric Sail
pages.text: Only makes drag, never lift. Angle it for turning or stabilising. On a windmill bearing it gives 0 RPM here; windmills need Windcatchers.

pages.title: A plane that flies
pages.text: [#](FFFFFF)[#]() **In depth.** A 15-block biplane 21 wide on Copycat Wings (8m) with a closed wooden body. Two Portable Engines behind the seats are geared to 256 RPM down to the wings' roots and out along them to four Wooden Propellers on the leading edge; two more engines, stacked behind the passenger, turn a Gyroscope at 256 RPM. It lifts off within 40 blocks, cruises near 17.5 blocks a second dead level and climbs past y 116. On sails it needs 27 across and cruises near 14.

A Steering Wheel at the seat steers it: a comparator at each side of the wheel slows one side's Analog Transmission while it is turned that way. Turn it briefly and back, since held over it spins and sinks. A Throttle Lever sets the speed through the same transmissions.

pages.title: Landing gear
pages.text: **Grindstones** roll almost freely as a plane's landing gear: one under the nose, two just behind the centre of mass. Offroad wheel mounts drag harder the faster they roll and the more weight they carry, so a plane on wheels needs far more wing and a long field. Planks and most blocks barely slide.

pages.title: Stopping and seeing
pages.text:
A **Gearshift** in each propeller line, on a lever at the pilot's hand, turns the propellers backwards after landing and stops a small plane in under 10 blocks.\
\
Keep engines and propellers behind the pilot or out on the wings, never in front of the windscreen.
